BC_description: Both `Promise.promisify`, `Promise.promisifyAll`, and `Promise.fromCallback` now by default only use the first argument passed to the callback adapter to resolve the promise. In Bluebird 2.x, if the callback received multiple values, the resolved result was an array of those values. In 3.x, only the first value is used by default. Code that expects an array as the resolved value will break unless the `{multiArgs: true}` option is provided.
Adaptation_method:
If you need the previous behavior (an array of callback arguments excluding the error), pass {multiArgs: true} as an option:

Before (2.x):
Promise.promisify(fs.stat)(file) // resolves with [stats, somethingElse]

After (3.x):
Promise.promisify(fs.stat, {multiArgs: true})(file)
// or using fromCallback:
Promise.fromCallback(cb, {multiArgs: true})

By default, only the first argument will be returned, so update usages accordingly to avoid bugs.
RequireInfo: The BC_description refers to both Promise.promisify, Promise.promisifyAll, and Promise.fromCallback. However, Promise.promisifyAll returns multiple methods and could involve multiple class or instance contexts, potentially affecting usages outside of just Promise. Clarification is needed regarding which objects' methods when promisified via promisifyAll are affected and if the internal context ('this') in promisified methods is impacted. Also, need explicit confirmation that {multiArgs: true} restores behavior identically for all three methods and whether signature/option handling differs in edge cases.
